messages.subject: colext - yearlySiteCovs for single-species multi-season model
parts:
Hello group,

I need help with understanding how the colext model reads the yearlySiteCovs input. If a study has t seasons, then there are always t-1 opportunities for inter-seasonal colonization/extinction events. If I want to model colonization/extinction using covariates, it seems I should only have t-1 columns of any given covariate hypothesized to influence inter-seasonal col/ext. Is that correct?

The reason I'm asking is that I originally entered t columns of each covariate instead of t-1, and the models fit just fine. But I'm not sure how the model treated the additional column. To be sure I was getting the right output, I removed the extra column for each covariate. Now, I'm receiving an error message when I try to create the unmarkedMultFrame (Error...At least one matrix in yearlySiteCovs has incorrect number of dimensions).

In my case, I've got 20 seasons of data. I'm trying to model the col/ext of the 19 inter-seasonal periods. 

Help? I must be missing something.

Thanks,
Gavin

Hi Gavin,

 

Yeah, I was about to suggest that perhaps the last column is ignored in this case where the t-1 data contributes to the transition probability from time t-1 to t. It means the same covariates can be used as year effects (on detection and occupancy) and for transition probabilities.

I’m not sure what you would do if you had a covariate that you were only interested in using for transition probabilities though – fill the last column with NAs or something?

 

Anyway, seems like you fixed it…

 

Chris
